grammar.label: the more … the more

explanation.en: Two comparatives in parallel show that one change drives another: 'The more you practise, the easier it becomes.'
explanation.uz: Ikki qiyosiy daraja yonma-yon kelib, bir o'zgarish ikkinchisini keltirib chiqarishini bildiradi: 'The more you practise, the easier it becomes.'

grammar.positive_example: The longer we waited, the angrier people got.
grammar.negative_example: More we waited, more people got angry.

l1_notes.uz: Ikkala qismda ham 'the' shart; o'zbekcha 'qancha… shuncha…' tuzilishiga to'g'ri keladi.

grammar.label: superlative + present perfect
grammar.form: the best … I have ever + past participle
grammar.meaning: ranking something against all your experience

explanation.en: Pair a superlative with 'I have ever': 'It is the best meal I have ever had.' The present perfect covers your whole life up to now.
explanation.uz: Ustunlik darajasi 'I have ever' bilan juftlashadi: 'It is the best meal I have ever had.' Present perfect butun umringizni hozirgacha qamraydi.

grammar.positive_example: That was the hardest exam I have ever taken.
grammar.negative_example: That was the hardest exam I ever took in my life until now.

l1_notes.uz: 'ever' inkor emas, 'hech qachon' emas — ijobiy gapda 'umringizda' degan ma'no beradi.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Look at this. Our numbers have risen every month since March.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is a sharp rise in June.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: The cheaper we made it, the more people came.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: The more people come, the more we spend on the hall.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: In the summer. The longer the season lasts, the better the year is.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: This is the clearest report I have ever seen from you.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Aziz drew the picture. I only gave him the numbers.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: It is the best year we have ever had.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then say that first, and show the picture second.
